metadata.title: The Collateral Impact of the Three-Dimensional Jacobian Counterexample: a Source-Verified Cascade
metadata.description:
On 2026-07-20, Levent Alpöge announced an explicit counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture in dimension 3, found working with the language model Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic). The credit for every consequence documented here belongs to that single map. This paper documents what else that map decides: through implication chains published over five decades, each re-verified against its primary source (EXP-001, EXP-016, EXP-018), the counterexample resolves or partially resolves the Mathieu conjecture, the Dixmier conjecture, the Poisson conjecture, the Gaussian moments conjecture, Zhao's vanishing conjecture, the Image conjecture, and the symmetric (gradient) form of the Jacobian conjecture. We state each corollary with its chain and its reference, list precisely what remains open, and describe the verification method, which turns a one-line certificate into a status map of a whole neighborhood of problems.

The symmetric/gradient and vanishing corollaries are made explicit: a non-invertible gradient Keller map id + grad f on C^48, with f a homogeneous Hessian-nilpotent quartic (382 monomials over Q(i)) and an exact two-point collision, built from Thompson's dimension-24 cubic-homogeneous form by the de Bondt-van den Essen construction and verified end to end in exact arithmetic.

Source code, data and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH (problems/algebraic-geometry/jacobian-conjecture).
metadata.version_notes: Revision. The text states the mathematics directly, without narrative about earlier revisions or the research programme: the abstract describes the explicit dimension-48 witness as a result of the paper, the first section is retitled The counterexample and its verification, the two corollaries point to the explicit witness directly, the difference from the nilpotency index stated in Thompson's source (18, not 17) is given as a fact, a closing paragraph of general advice is removed, and the closing method note becomes a method and data-availability section that states what the EXP identifiers denote. The record title now matches the title printed in the paper. The title is set on balanced lines, a long repository path in the references no longer stretches its line, the reference labels are aligned, and a page-1 header block states the document type, version, licence and DOIs. Corrections. (1) Corollary 3 (Dixmier) is corrected. Dixmier(n) implies JC(n), so Dixmier(n) is false for every n ≥ 3, and ranks 1 and 2 remain open. The previous text concluded that Dixmier(2) is false from the falsity of JC(4), which the implication from JC(2n) to Dixmier(n) does not support; the list of open problems now names ranks 1 and 2. (2) The Gaussian moments corollary now cites the explicit three-variable counterexample of C. D. Long (arXiv:2607.18186): the moments conjecture is false in every dimension n ≥ 3, and only the dimensions below 3 remain open. (3) The statement that the paper contains no original mathematics now separates the corollaries, which compose published implications, from the explicit witness of Section 3, a construction from published ingredients. (4) The announcement date is 2026-07-20 and the model is named as in the announcement (Claude Fable 5). Methods, data and the other results are unchanged.
